newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia debt not affected by rupiah fall - paper.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia debt not affected by rupiah fall - paper.

text.p: Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita has said Indonesia's external debt will not rise significantly due to the rupiah's decline against the U.S. dollar, the official Antara news agency said on Monday.
He was quoted as saying much of the foreign debt, totalling more than $100 million, was denominated in Japanese yen.
The rupiah fell sharply and closed in Jakarta at an historic low of 2,900 against the dollar on Friday. The currency has lost more than 20 percent of its value so far this year.
"The rise (in debt) is not high," Ginanjar told reporters on Sunday after attending celebrations marking the country's 52nd anniversary of independence.
He said the cause of the appreciation of the dollar against regional currencies, including the rupiah, could not be separated from the improvement in the U.S. economy.
"The U.S. economy under President Bill Clinton is the best over the last decade," he said.
He also said the government hoped small businesses could take advantage of the rupiah's fall to boost export competitiveness.
